definitions.explanation: The essential or most important quality of something, especially an art, discipline, or tradition. Emphasizes the deepest, most fundamental aspect that defines its true nature.

examples.japanese: ⟦{武道|ぶどう}→武道：09640_budou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{神髄|しんずい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{学|まな}ぶ→学ぶ：01987_manabu⟧。
examples.english: To learn the essence of martial arts.

examples.japanese: ⟦{長年|ながねん}→長年：09684_naganen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{修行|しゅぎょう}→修行：05522_shugyou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{経|へ}て→経る：13876_heru⟧、ようやく⟦{茶道|さどう}→茶道：04451_sadou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{神髄|しんずい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{触|ふ}れた→触れる：01984_fureru⟧。
examples.english: After many years of training, I finally touched upon the true spirit of the tea ceremony.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{一冊|いっさつ}→一冊：23149_issatsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{伝統|でんとう}{芸能|げいのう}→伝統芸能：15098_dentougeinou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{神髄|しんずい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦わかりやすく→わかりやすい：09582_wakariyasui⟧⟦まとめられている→まとめる：02424_matomeru⟧。
examples.english: This book concisely summarizes the essence of Japan's traditional performing arts.

notes:
USAGE:
Used to describe the deepest, most essential quality of a discipline, art, philosophy, or tradition. Often appears in contexts involving mastery or deep understanding achieved through long study or practice. More literary and elevated in register than simply saying ⟦{本質|ほんしつ}→本質：04810_honshitsu⟧ (essence).
Similar to ⟦{真髄|しんずい}→真髄：13671_shinzui⟧ (same reading, different first kanji). Both words mean "essence" and are sometimes used interchangeably, but {神髄|しんずい} carries a slightly more spiritual or sacred nuance (using the kanji for "god/spirit"), while ⟦{真髄|しんずい}→真髄：13671_shinzui⟧ emphasizes truth and authenticity (using the kanji for "true").

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {神髄|しんずい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{触|ふ}れる→触れる：01984_fureru⟧: to come into contact with the essence
- {神髄|しんずい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{極|きわ}める→極める：13139_kiwameru⟧: to master the essence
- {神髄|しんずい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{伝|つた}える→伝える：01220_tsutaeru⟧: to convey the essence

cross_references.description: Similar word with same reading but different nuance
